title: The third clause in Theorem 2.15 uses f where the witness is g.
details: In arXiv2210.17333v3, Theorem2.15 proof condition(III) reads that if both indexed sets are empty, then f(i,j) is outside C union D. The proof has fixed a weak double coproductivity witness g, and f has not been defined there. Replace f(i,j) by g(i,j); the later definition h(y)=g(f1(y),f2(y)) and its neither-side case then use exactly this corrected clause. This is a local symbol slip, not a failure of the universality argument. The corpus uses the direct effective-inseparability singleton-enlargement proof rather than adopting this clause verbatim.
